title: The Spring Listing Surge: Why Real Estate Agencies Feel Busiest When Cash Is Tightest
linkedin:
Spring is real estate agencies' busiest listing season, and often their tightest for cash, at exactly the same time.

The mechanics are simple once you see them. A new listing gets a marketing campaign, photography, signboards, digital ads, paid for close to the moment it is booked. The commission that campaign is meant to earn does not land until the property sells and settles, commonly weeks or even a couple of months later.

So an agency can be running its strongest listing volume of the year and still feel the cash squeeze hardest in the same six or eight weeks. That is not a sign anything has gone wrong. It is simply what happens when marketing spend and staffing costs front-run settlement income during a fast seasonal ramp-up.

What softens it is having a steady property management book underneath the sales desk. Rent roll income arrives monthly regardless of how many listings are on the board, giving the agency a floor to stand on while sales commission moves in lumps.

The agencies that ride out spring calmly are not the ones with less marketing spend. They are the ones who have mapped, week by week, exactly where the gap opens and funded it on purpose, rather than discovering it once the campaigns are already booked.

Full piece on the ProfitPulse blog.
